study_identification.title: Shared differential factors underlying individual spontaneous neural activity abnormalities in major depressive disorder

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Associations tested between factor compositions and clinical features (episodicity, medication status, HAMD scores), plus neurobiological mappings (neurotransmitter receptor/transporters, inflammation-related gene transcription profiles, SC-informed epicenters).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Identified two positive and two negative differential factors capturing individualized ALFF deviations in MDD; factors relate to symptoms and neurobiology and enable four reproducible subtypes; results replicate across independent multi-site datasets and atlas choices.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: GPR-based normative modeling on HCs produced per-ROI ALFF Z-scores for patients. NMF decomposed individualized abnormalities into four factors (two positive, two negative) explaining ~57% variance. Factors correlated with clinical measures (higher HAMD with positive factors; lower with negative), differed by episodicity and medication, and mapped to distinct neurotransmitter and inflammation gene profiles and SC-informed epicenters. Group-level abnormalities were well explained by factor compositions (adj. R2 ~0.71 discovery; ~0.68 validation). Robustness confirmed via 10-fold CV, LOSO CV, cross-dataset generalization, and alternate atlas (AAL).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: No explicit model-based handling of site/scanner effects in the normative model; software implementation not specified; cross-sectional design limits causal inference; preprocessing differences across datasets may introduce residual confounds despite validation.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Factor compositions may support stratification of MDD into neurobiologically relevant subtypes. Normative modeling of ALFF shows generalizable performance but requires explicit site handling and standardized pipelines for potential clinical translation.

general_notes.general_notes: Primary atlas appears to be Brainnetome (246 regions); AAL (90 regions, excluding cerebellum) used for sensitivity. Acquisition on 3.0T GE/Siemens; preprocessing includes motion regression (Friston-24), WM/CSF regression, scrubbing (discovery), MNI normalization (EPI/DARTEL), 0.01-0.1 Hz filtering, 6mm smoothing (discovery). Group-level tests control for age, sex, site, and mean FD.
